patients.summary: Retired accountant with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia and mild asthma who joins in 2017; over nine years he develops mild cognitive impairment, an ACE-inhibitor cough, BPH with retention, cervical myelopathy, heart failure, an inferior STEMI and two strokes, the last after his final practice visit. Outside records arrive late or not at all.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
65 yo retired accountant transferring care; his old office is closing its Medicare panel. Wife at home, son lives nearby in town.

PMH: type 2 diabetes for roughly 13 years, on metformin 1000 twice a day and glyburide 5 each morning. HTN for many years, always called borderline, kept to diet; never put on a pill. High cholesterol on atorvastatin 40. Asthma since his 30s, mild, uses albuterol a handful of times a year, mostly with colds. Aspirin 81 daily, was told years ago it was for the heart.
PSH: none.
Allergies: none to medicines.
FH: father, heart attack at 61. Mother had type 2 diabetes. Brother had an ischemic stroke at 65.
SH: never smoked. A drink or two a month. Married. Walks most mornings.

ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, polyuria, foot numbness, vision change beyond needing new readers.

Exam: well appearing, pleasant. BP as charted, recheck similar. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Feet: intact skin, pulses 2+, monofilament normal both feet.

A/P
1. T2DM: A1c, CMP, urine microalbumin today. Same regimen pending results.
2. HTN: just over goal for a diabetic. He would rather keep working on salt and walking than add a pill. Recheck at each visit.
3. Hyperlipidemia: lipid panel today, continue atorvastatin 40.
4. Mild intermittent asthma: albuterol as needed, refills on file.
5. Health maintenance: records release signed for his prior office (colonoscopy and vaccine history). PHQ-2 0.
Follow up 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Archambault, your labs are back. A1c is about where your old office had it, kidney and liver tests are fine, blood count normal, no protein in the urine. Cholesterol numbers are similar to before on the atorvastatin. Nothing to change right now. See you in July.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records from former primary care office received by fax, 38 pages, scanned.

Highlights abstracted for the PCP:
- Screening colonoscopy 2015: normal to the cecum, no polyps. Repeat in 10 years was suggested.
- PCV13 2016, PPSV23 2017 (February).
- Hepatitis C antibody 2016: nonreactive.
- Problem list matches what he gave us. Blood pressures over the past 3 years mostly 130s/80s, never treated.
- Last A1c there 7.0.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:

O: vitals as charted. Feet look fine. Lungs clear.

A/P: T2DM - point of care A1c sent, will message. HTN - similar to April, still prefers no drug, fair enough for now. Eye exam due, he will book with his optometrist. RTC 4 months for wellness visit.

Cognition: no concerns raised by patient or wife (she came along). Mini-Cog not done today.
Home safety: lives in a two-story house, railings in place.
PHQ-2 negative.
Prevention: colonoscopy 2015 normal. Pneumococcal series complete. Flu done in October. Shingrix discussed - he wants to wait until after the eye surgery.
Advance directive: thinking about naming his wife and son, handed him the health care proxy form.

Chronic: T2DM and HTN stable. Labs today. Plan reviewed in writing.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Planned procedure: right cataract extraction with lens implant, outpatient, monitored anesthesia care. Date per surgeon late January.

No chest pain or dyspnea, climbs two flights without stopping. Asthma quiet. No bleeding problems.
Exam: heart regular, lungs clear.
ECG today normal sinus.
Labs from November reviewed, fine.

Assessment: low risk patient for low risk procedure. OK to proceed.
Meds: hold metformin and glyburide the morning of surgery since he will be NPO, resume with first meal. Continue aspirin per the surgeon's usual practice. Bring albuterol.
Form faxed to the surgery center.

orders.reason: mild cognitive impairment, confirm and follow

documents.title: Chronic Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Son came along today.

S: Leonard says he feels well and has nothing new. Taking everything as prescribed, pillbox kept by his wife. His son, out of his father's earshot at first and then with him, says Dad repeats stories and has lost track of a couple of appointments (May no-show) and once left the stove on. Leonard thinks it is just getting older.
On direct questions about the urinary side: up 2 to 3 times a night for a couple of years, slow stream, some waiting to start. No dysuria. He had not thought to mention it.

O: BP 132/84, repeat similar. Exam unremarkable: heart regular, lungs clear, no edema, feet intact, gait normal, no focal neuro findings.
MoCA 23/30 (lost points on delayed recall and clock). Fasting labs today.

A/P
1. Memory: MoCA 23 fits mild cognitive impairment. Checking B12 and TSH. Referral to neurology to confirm and follow. Talked with both about keeping the pillbox and calendar system.
2. HTN with diabetes: still above 130/80 after two years of diet. Starting lisinopril 20 mg daily. BMP in 2 weeks with the other results.
3. LUTS, likely BPH: PSA today. Start tamsulosin 0.4 at bedtime, warned about standing slowly at night.
4. T2DM: A1c today; glyburide/metformin unchanged.
5. Hyperlipidemia: lipids today on atorvastatin 40.
Follow up 6 to 8 weeks for BP.

documents.title: Results from Tuesday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hello Leonard (and Marc, since you are on the proxy now), results are in. A1c 7.2, fasting sugar 154: a bit above goal but steady. LDL 145 with HDL 35 and triglycerides 200. B12, thyroid and PSA are normal, kidney function normal. Nothing here explains the memory changes, which is reassuring, and neurology should call you within a few weeks. Keep taking the new blood pressure pill and the tamsulosin; we will see you in late September.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Cough
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back for BP follow-up and a cough. Dry, tickly cough for about 4 weeks, no phlegm. Denies shortness of breath, fever, chills, weight loss. Not wheezy; tried albuterol twice, no difference. Lisinopril started here 6 to 7 weeks ago. Wife says the cough wakes them both.
CXR from an insurance exam this past week is in the chart: clear.

Exam: afebrile. Breath sounds normal throughout, expiratory phase slightly long, no wheeze, no crackles or rales. Heart regular, no murmur. No JVD, no leg edema.

A/P
1. Cough from lisinopril, near certain by timing and a clear film. Stop lisinopril. Recorded as an ACE inhibitor intolerance. Can take a few weeks to settle.
2. HTN: start amlodipine 5 mg daily. Ankle swelling possible, call if so.
3. Asthma: not active, no change.
Nurse BP check with his flu shot in about a week.

documents.title: Flu vaccine and BP check
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu R deltoid. BP on amlodipine as charted, at goal. Cough is "half what it was." No ankle swelling. Reviewed with PCP, no changes.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outpatient neurology group. Date of service 11/20/2019.
Reason for referral: memory concerns raised by family.

History: 68 year old man, retired accountant, accompanied by his son. About 6 to 9 months of repeating questions and misplacing appointments. Still manages finances with his wife double checking. No hallucinations, no change in personality, no gait change, no tremor.
PMH: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, mild asthma.
Meds: metformin, glyburide, amlodipine, atorvastatin, aspirin, tamsulosin, albuterol as needed.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough).

Exam: alert, attentive. Language fluent. Cranial nerves intact. Strength full, tone normal, reflexes symmetric, plantar responses flexor. Gait and tandem normal.
Cognitive screen in clinic: deficits mainly in delayed recall, executive items intact enough for daily function.
PCP labs (B12, TSH) reviewed and normal.

Impression: mild cognitive impairment, amnestic predominant. Instrumental activities preserved.
Plan: no medication at this stage. Cardiovascular risk control, exercise, social engagement. Return yearly or sooner for change.

documents.title: Son calling re hospital stay
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Son Marc called. Dad could not pass urine last week, went to the regional hospital ED, catheter put in and he was kept overnight. Catheter came out the next morning and he voided before discharge. Told to see urology. They did not get any paperwork to bring us.
Currently voiding, slow stream, no fever. Still on tamsulosin.
Per PCP: urology referral placed today. Records request faxed to the hospital.

reports.text: Transabdominal ultrasound of the urinary bladder before and after voiding. Bladder wall smooth. No intraluminal mass or stone. Prostate impresses on the bladder base and is enlarged by volume estimate. Post-void residual 220 mL.

documents.title: Urology consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology practice. Date of visit 01/27/2020.

Reason: lower urinary tract symptoms worse after a retention episode.

HPI: 68 yo man with hypertension, diabetes and memory impairment, recent cough attributed to lisinopril, referred by his PCP. Nocturia 3 to 4 times nightly, weak stream, urgency, trouble getting started. Two episodes of painless visible blood in the urine over the past few months. Required catheterization last month during an overnight admission for acute retention. Tamsulosin begun about six months ago by his PCP helped initially, but the symptoms have crept back.
PMH: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, mild asthma.
Meds (per patient list): metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glyburide 5 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, albuterol HFA as needed, tamsulosin 0.4 mg.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough).

Exam: vitals normal. Abdomen soft, bladder not palpable. DRE: prostate firm, symmetrically enlarged, no nodules, nontender.
Labs: creatinine normal.
Imaging: bladder ultrasound last week, enlarged prostate by volume, PVR 220 mL.

Assessment: BPH with LUTS, symptoms recurring on alpha blocker monotherapy, with a retention episode and visible hematuria.
Plan:
- Add finasteride 5 mg daily to tamsulosin; expect benefit over 3 to 6 months.
- Hematuria evaluation: renal ultrasound and office cystoscopy.
- Return after cystoscopy.

reports.text: Right kidney 11.2 cm, left kidney 11.5 cm. Normal cortical thickness and echogenicity. No hydronephrosis, stone or mass either side. Bladder partially distended, unremarkable.

documents.title: Urology procedure note and imaging
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Office flexible cystoscopy, 02/19/2020. Topical lidocaine. Urethra normal. Prostatic urethra narrowed by enlarged lateral lobes. Bladder wall normal, no tumor, stone or diverticulum, ureteral orifices normal. Tolerated well.
Renal ultrasound 02/14/2020: normal kidneys, no hydronephrosis.
Impression: hematuria likely prostatic in origin; no bladder lesion.
Plan: continue tamsulosin plus finasteride. Recheck in 6 months. Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough).

documents.body: Called wife: April in-person visit changed to video given the pandemic. Son will help with the tablet. She asked about refills; all on file through June.

Home BP cuff readings 120s to 130s over 70s to 80s. Cough from the spring is gone. Urinating better since finasteride was added, up twice a night. No visible blood since February.
No hypoglycemia. Not much walking lately; encouraged laps around the yard.
A/P: HTN controlled on amlodipine. BPH per urology. T2DM - lab-only visit for A1c and BMP next week, masked, early morning slot. Med list updated with finasteride from urology. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Diabetes check. Says he is fine, but his wife brings up that his legs have been stiff since summer and he has tripped on the stairs a few times, caught the railing each time. Also his fingers feel numb, buttons are harder, dropped a mug last week. No neck pain to speak of. No bladder change beyond the prostate symptoms he already has.

O: BP at goal. Gait a bit stiff and wide. Grip seems weaker on both sides. Leg reflexes brisk. Did not go further today.

A/P
1. Leg stiffness, falls and hand numbness: new since his neurology visit and needs their exam. He has a yearly neurology follow-up next month anyway; called their office and they will add the gait and hand symptoms to the visit. Fall precautions reviewed, railings, night lights.
2. T2DM: A1c and fasting glucose today. Glyburide noted with his age, but no lows, continue.
3. HLD: lipids today on atorvastatin 40.
4. HTN: continue amlodipine.
RTC 3 months, sooner after neurology.

documents.title: Neurology appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, this is Marc writing for my dad. Neurology called and has him on Feb 9. Do they need anything from you before then? Also are his blood tests back?

documents.title: RE: Neurology appointment
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Marc. I sent them my note from Tuesday, so they know about the walking and the hands. Labs: A1c 7.2, fasting sugar 156, LDL 130, HDL 45, triglycerides 150, kidney tests normal. Same ballpark as before. Neurology can see these too.

reports.text:
Technique: sagittal and axial T1 and T2 sequences of the cervical spine without contrast.
Findings: alignment maintained. Multilevel degenerative disc disease and uncovertebral and facet hypertrophy from C3 to C7. At C5-C6, disc osteophyte complex and ligamentous thickening narrow the spinal canal. Other levels without significant canal narrowing. Craniocervical junction normal. Paraspinal soft tissues unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Multilevel cervical degenerative changes with spinal canal narrowing at C5-C6.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outpatient neurology group. Date of service 02/09/2021.

Return visit for mild cognitive impairment, with new gait and hand complaints raised by his PCP.
HPI: About 6 months of progressive trouble walking and numb hands. Legs feel stiff; he has tripped several times. Memory per son unchanged since 2019.
PMH: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hypercholesterolemia, mild asthma, BPH.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glyburide 5 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, albuterol HFA as needed.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough).

Exam: grip strength reduced both hands with wasting of the intrinsic hand muscles. Upper limb reflexes diminished. Lower limb reflexes brisk. Babinski sign present on both sides. Gait spastic.
Recent labs from PCP (01/19/2021): A1c 7.2%, fasting glucose 156, total cholesterol 210, LDL 130, HDL 45, triglycerides 150.
MRI cervical spine (02/02/2021): multilevel degenerative change with canal narrowing at C5-C6.

Impression: cervical spondylotic myelopathy at C5-C6. MCI stable.
Plan: referral to spine surgery to discuss decompression. Fall precautions. Avoid neck manipulation. Return 6 months.

events.reason: Follow-up after neurology and spine surgery

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: cervical myelopathy, gait and hand function, fall prevention

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With son. Saw the spine surgeon in April (we never got a letter; second request sent today). Per Leonard and Marc: the surgeon offered a neck decompression, explained the aim is to stop things getting worse. Leonard decided against surgery for now. Marc supports him, though worried. They would like therapy.
No new weakness since February by their account. No bowel or bladder change beyond his known BPH. One more stumble, no fall.
Exam: spastic gait, uses the rail for the exam step. Hand grip weak both sides. Unchanged from neurology's description.
A/P
1. Cervical myelopathy, nonoperative by his choice: PT referral for gait, balance and hand work. Return precautions given clearly to both: any rapid change in walking, hands or bladder, call the same day. Neurology following.
2. Other problems stable. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Physical therapy initial evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
Outpatient PT. Evaluation 05/25/2021.
Dx: cervical spondylotic myelopathy.
Subjective: stiff legs, trips on stairs, clumsy hands. Goal: keep walking the neighborhood safely.
Objective: spastic gait pattern, reduced stride length. Single-leg stance under 5 s each side. Timed Up and Go 14 s. Grip reduced bilaterally.
Plan: 2x/week for 8 weeks; balance, gait training, lower extremity strengthening, fine motor work. Home program issued. Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough).

orders.reason: progressive exertional dyspnea and bilateral leg edema, urgent

documents.title: Dyspnea and Edema
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Since about May, more winded with exertion: now stops halfway up the stairs, used to manage the hill on his street. Both ankles swell by evening. Denies chest pain, palpitations, fainting. Not wheezy, albuterol does nothing for it. Weight up a few pounds without eating more.

O: BP and weight as charted. Heart regular. Lungs: I hear no wheeze. Ankle edema both sides.
ECG in office: sinus, no acute change.

A/P: exertional dyspnea with edema in a 71 yo diabetic with hypertension: heart failure is the leading concern. Amlodipine can swell ankles but would not explain the breathlessness. Urgent cardiology referral, spoke with their scheduler for a slot in about 2 weeks. ED precautions given: chest pain, breathlessness at rest, unable to lie flat. Wife repeated them back.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning

reports.text: PA and lateral. The cardiac silhouette is enlarged. Pulmonary vascular cephalization. No focal consolidation. No pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Cardiomegaly with cephalization of the pulmonary vasculature.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Date of visit 08/10/2022.

Referred for: exertional dyspnea and leg swelling.
HPI: 71 yo man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, a prior cough on lisinopril and cervical myelopathy. Three months of steadily worse breathlessness on exertion and swelling of both legs. No chest pain, palpitations or syncope.
Meds: metformin, amlodipine, atorvastatin, glyburide 5 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, aspirin 81 mg, albuterol as needed.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary

Regional hospital, cardiology service. Admitted 08/01/2024, discharged 08/04/2024.

Principal diagnosis: acute ST elevation MI, inferior wall, right coronary artery.
Procedure 08/01: emergent coronary angiography via right radial artery. Acute RCA occlusion; primary PCI with one drug-eluting stent, TIMI 3 flow. Other vessels without flow-limiting disease.
Course: chest pain resolved after PCI. Monitored in the CCU overnight, no arrhythmia. Echo 08/02: LVEF 50%, inferior hypokinesis. Ambulating independently with cane by day 2.

Discharge medications:
- Aspirin 81 mg daily
- Clopidogrel 75 mg daily for at least 12 months (chosen over ticagrelor given age and fall risk)
- Atorvastatin 80 mg daily (increased from 40)
- Metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily (new)
- Continue furosemide 40 mg, empagliflozin 10 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, metformin, glyburide, tamsulosin, finasteride, albuterol as needed
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough).

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week, cardiology 6 weeks, cardiac rehab referral sent. Do not stop clopidogrel without speaking to cardiology.

Course: no bleeding after thrombolysis. Speech normal by day 2. Left arm and leg strength much improved; mild left hand weakness and clumsiness at discharge. Noted on reconciliation that he was already on aspirin and clopidogrel (12-month course after 2024 RCA stent, about to end).

Discharge plan:
- Aspirin 81 mg plus clopidogrel 75 mg together for 90 days from the stroke, then aspirin alone.
- Atorvastatin 80 mg daily.
- Other home medications unchanged.
- Outpatient physical and occupational therapy.
- No driving until cleared.
- Follow up with PCP in 1 week, neurology in 3 months.
